butir.teks: The Merit of Knowledge
Its evidences from the Qur'an: the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ⟦QS 3:18⟧ Consider

how Allah, glorified and exalted is He, began with Himself, put the angels second, and put the people of knowledge third. That is enough for you as honour, merit, splendour, and nobility! And Allah Most High says ⟦QS 58:11⟧ Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) said: "The scholars have degrees above the believers by seven hundred degrees, and between each two degrees is a journey of five hundred years."

And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says ⟦QS 39:9⟧, and Allah Most High says ⟦QS 35:28⟧, and Allah Most High says ⟦QS 13:43⟧, and Allah Most High says ⟦QS 27:40⟧, to draw attention to the fact that he became capable through the power of knowledge.
And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says ⟦QS 28:80⟧. He made clear that the greatness of the worth of the Hereafter is known through knowledge.

And Allah Most High says ⟦QS 29:43⟧, and Allah Most High says ⟦QS 4:83⟧. He referred His ruling in cases that occur to their deduction, and joined their rank to the rank of the prophets in uncovering the ruling of Allah.
It was said concerning the saying of Allah Most High ⟦QS 7:26⟧ saw'atikum means knowledge, rishan means certainty, and libas at-taqwa means modesty.

And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says ⟦QS 7:52⟧, and Allah Most High says ⟦QS 7:7⟧, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says ⟦QS 29:49⟧, and Allah Most High says ⟦QS 55:3-4⟧. He mentioned that only in the context of reminding of favour.

As for the reports, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever Allah wishes good for, He gives him understanding of the religion and inspires him with his right guidance" (١). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The scholars are the heirs of the prophets" (٢). And it is known that there is no rank above prophethood and no honour above the honour of inheriting that rank.

And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whatever is in the heavens and the earth asks forgiveness for the scholar" (٣). And what position is higher than the position of one for whom the angels of the heavens and the earth busy themselves with asking forgiveness?

And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Wisdom increases the noble in honour and raises the slave until he reaches the levels of kings" (٤). With this he drew attention to its fruits in this world, and it is known that the Hereafter is better and more lasting.

And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Two traits do not exist in a hypocrite: good bearing and understanding of the religion (fiqh)" (٥). Do not doubt the hadith because of the hypocrisy of some jurists of the age, for he did not mean by it the fiqh you supposed. The meaning of fiqh will come.

The lowest degree of the jurist (faqih) is that he knows that the Hereafter is better than this world. When this knowledge is genuine and prevails over him, he is cleared by it of hypocrisy and showing off (riya').

And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The best of people is the believing scholar who, if he is needed, benefits, and if he is dispensed with, makes himself self-sufficient" (٦). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Faith is naked; its clothing is God-consciousness (taqwa), its adornment is modesty, and its fruit is knowledge" (٧). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The nearest of people to the degree of prophethood are the people of knowledge and jihad. As for the people of knowledge, they guided people to what the messengers brought; and as for the people of jihad, they struggled with their swords."
to what the messengers brought (١)

And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The death of a tribe is easier than the death of a scholar" (٢). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "People are mines, like the mines of gold and silver; the best of them in the Jahiliyya are the best of them in Islam, if they gain understanding" (٣). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The ink of the scholars will be weighed against the blood of the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection" (٤). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever preserves for my community forty hadiths of the Sunna until he delivers them to them, I will be an intercessor and a witness for him on the Day of Resurrection" (٥). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever of my community carries forty hadiths will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection as a jurist and a scholar" (٦). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever gains understanding in the religion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Allah Most High will suffice him in what concerns him and will provide for him from where he does not expect" (٧). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Abraham (peace be upon him): 'O Abraham, I am Knowing, and I love everyone who is knowing'" (٨). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The scholar is the trustee of Allah, glorified is He, on earth" (٩). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Two groups of my community: if they are righteous, people are righteous, and if they are corrupt, people are corrupt: the rulers and the jurists" (١٠). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If a day comes upon me in which I do not increase in knowledge that brings me nearer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then may there be no blessing for me in the rising of the sun of that day" (١١). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, on the preference of knowledge over worship and martyrdom: "The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over the lowest man among my Companions" (١٢). Consider how he made knowledge accompany the degree of prophethood, and how he lowered the rank of action stripped of knowledge, even though the worshipper is not without knowledge of the worship he persists in, and without it there would be no worship. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon on the night of the full moon over the rest of the stars" (١٣). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Three will intercede on the Day of Resurrection: the prophets, then the scholars, then the martyrs" (١٤). How great a rank it is, one that follows prophethood and is above martyrdom, even with what has been reported about the merit of martyrdom!

The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Allah Most High is not worshipped with anything better than understanding in the religion (fiqh); and one jurist is harder on Satan than a thousand worshippers; and everything has a pillar, and the pillar of this religion is fiqh" (١٥). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The best of your religion is the easiest of it, and the best worship is fiqh" (١٦). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The superiority of the believing scholar over

the believing worshipper by seventy degrees (١). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "You have come to be in a time whose jurists are many, whose reciters and preachers are few, whose askers are few, and whose givers are many; action in it is better than knowledge. And there will come upon people a time whose jurists are few, whose preachers are many, whose givers are few, and whose askers are many; knowledge in it is better than action" (٢). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Between the scholar and the worshipper are a hundred degrees; between each two degrees is the running of a swift, conditioned horse for seventy years" (٣). And it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, which deed is best?" He said: "Knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Then it was said: "Which knowledge do you mean?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Knowledge of Allah, glorified is He." Then it was said to him: "We ask about action and you answer about knowledge." So he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A little action benefits with knowledge of Allah, and a great deal of action does not benefit with ignorance of Allah" (٤). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah, glorified is He, will raise the servants, then He will raise the scholars, then He will say: 'O assembly of scholars, I did not place My knowledge in you except because of My knowledge of you, and I did not place My knowledge in you in order to punish you. Go, for I have forgiven you'" (٥). We ask Allah for a good ending.

As for the reports (athar), Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Kumayl: "O Kumayl, knowledge is better than wealth. Knowledge guards you, while you guard wealth. Knowledge is a ruler, and wealth is ruled over. Wealth is diminished by spending, while knowledge grows through spending."

And Ali also said (may Allah be pleased with him): "The scholar is better than the one who fasts, prays at night, and strives in jihad. And when the scholar dies, a breach is made in Islam that only a successor of his kind can close." And he (may Allah be pleased with him) said in verse:

Pride belongs only to the people of knowledge;
they are guides to guidance for whoever seeks guidance.

The worth of every man is what he does well,
and the ignorant are enemies of the people of knowledge.

So win knowledge and you will live by it forever;
people are dead, and the people of knowledge are alive.

And Abu al-Aswad said: "Nothing is more precious than knowledge. Kings are rulers over people, and scholars are rulers over kings." And Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) said: "Solomon son of David (peace be upon them) was given a choice between knowledge, wealth, and kingship, and he chose knowledge, so he was given wealth and kingship along with it." Ibn al-Mubarak was asked: "Who are the people?" He said: "The scholars." It was said: "Then who are the kings?" He said: "The renunciants (zuhhad)." It was said: "Then who are the lowly?" He said: "Those who eat this world by means of religion." And he did not count anyone other than the scholar as among the people, because the distinguishing quality by which people are set apart from the rest of the beasts is knowledge. So the human being is human by that for the sake of which he is noble. That is not through the strength of his body, for the camel is stronger than he; nor through his size, for the elephant is bigger than he; nor through his courage, for the beast of prey is braver than he; nor through his eating, for the ox has a wider belly than he; nor in order to have intercourse, for the lowliest of sparrows is stronger than he at mating. Rather, he was created only for knowledge.
And one of the scholars said: "I wish I knew what the one who has missed knowledge has attained, and what the one who has attained knowledge has missed."

And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever is given the Qur'an and thinks that anyone has been given something better than it has belittled what Allah Most High has magnified." And Fath al-Mawsili (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Does not a sick person die if food, drink, and medicine are withheld from him?" They said: "Yes." He said: "In the same way the heart dies if wisdom and knowledge are withheld from it for three days."

He spoke the truth, for the nourishment of the heart is knowledge and wisdom, and through them is its life, just as the nourishment of the body is food. Whoever loses knowledge, his heart is sick and his death is inevitable, but he does not feel it, since love of this world

and his preoccupation with it nullified his awareness, just as the overpowering of fear may nullify the pain of wounds at the moment, even though it is real. Then, when death puts down from him the burdens of this world, he feels his ruin and grieves with great regret, and then it does not benefit him. That is like the awareness of the one who has become safe from his fear, and of the one who has sobered up from his drunkenness, of the wounds that befell him while drunk or afraid. So we seek refuge in Allah from the day the covering is removed. For people are asleep, and when they die they awaken. And al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "The ink of the scholars is weighed against the blood of the martyrs, and the ink of the scholars outweighs the blood of the martyrs."

And Ibn Masud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Hold fast to knowledge before it is taken away, and its being taken away is the death of its transmitters. By Him in whose hand is my soul, men who were killed in the cause of Allah as martyrs will certainly wish that Allah would raise them as scholars, because of what they see of their honour. For no one is born a scholar; knowledge comes only through learning."

And Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) said: "Discussing knowledge together for part of a night is dearer to me than spending all of it in worship." And likewise from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) and Ahmad ibn Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on him).
And al-Hasan said, regarding the saying of Allah Most High ⟦QS 2:201⟧: "The good in this world is knowledge and worship, and in the Hereafter it is Paradise."

And one of the wise was asked: "Which things should one acquire?" He said: "The things that, if your ship sinks, swim with you," meaning knowledge. And it was said that by the sinking of the ship he meant the destruction of one's body through death.
And one of them said: "Whoever takes wisdom as a bridle, people take him as a leader; and whoever is known for wisdom, eyes watch him with reverence."

And al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Part of the nobility of knowledge is that everyone who is ascribed to it, even in something insignificant, rejoices, and whoever has it removed from him grieves."

And Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O people, hold fast to knowledge, for Allah, glorified is He, has a cloak that He loves. Whoever seeks a door of knowledge, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, clothes him with His cloak. If he commits a sin, He asks him three times to make amends, so that He will not strip him of that cloak of His, even if that sin goes on with him until he dies."
And al-Ahnaf (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "The scholars almost became lords, and every honour not founded on knowledge ends in disgrace."

And Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd said: "My master bought me for three hundred dirhams and freed me. I said: By what shall I make a living? So I took up knowledge as a trade, and a year had not been completed for me before the governor of Medina came to me as a visitor, and I did not give him permission."

And al-Zubayr ibn Abi Bakr said: "My father wrote to me in Iraq: Hold fast to knowledge, for if you become poor, it will be wealth for you, and if you become rich, it will be beauty for you." And that was related in the counsels of Luqman to his son. He said: "O my son, sit with the scholars and press close to them with your knees, for Allah, glorified is He, gives life to hearts with the light of wisdom, as He gives life to the earth with the downpour of the sky."
And one of the wise said: "When the scholar dies, the fish in the water and the bird in the air weep for him; his face is missed, and his mention is not forgotten."
And al-Zuhri (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Knowledge is male, and only the males among men love it."
